text:
Eetu Luostarinen has two Stanley Cup rings and one of the least glamorous jobs on the Panthers. He kills penalties, blocks shots (26 already), and draws the other team's best players: Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 94th percentile last season, and still had him at 1.6 wins above replacement, 79th among 401 forwards.

The points haven't come this season: five in 21 games and no goals in his last ten. His own chance rate has slipped from 0.68 individual expected goals per 60 to 0.47, and he's shooting 8.7%. Nothing here screams bad luck; it's a third-line checker who isn't getting many looks.

The ice is still tilting his way, though. Florida takes 54% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, three points better than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking catches something you can watch for: 24% of his setups came from behind the net last season, against 8% for a typical forward, and 62% of his exits left the zone with possession. If you're watching Florida, look for him behind the goal line.
